title: Client-signed usage certificates for idempotent ingest and provisional quota reservations
creator: Lena Patel
description:
Problem: At-least-once client retries (network timeouts, service restarts, SDK retries) can cause duplicate billable ingestion events and transient quota double-counting. Existing heuristics (short-lived client nonces, server-side heuristics) fail for long-tail retries and multi-path ingress (API gateway -> edge proxies -> regional routers).

Proposal: introduce a compact, client-signed Usage Certificate that the client includes with every logical request. The certificate contains a deterministic payload digest, client id, monotonic counter or locally-unique nonce, estimated token/license usage, and a TTL timestamp. The client signs the certificate with the API secret (HMAC) or an asymmetric key where available. Servers verify the signature and atomically check/record the certificate in a per-customer ledger with states (provisional,resolved,rolled_back). Provisional reservation allows immediate quota checks and provisional billing liability; finalization occurs on the response path to commit actual tokens consumed. This enables safe retry semantics: identical certificates are deduplicated server-side, and retries of in-flight requests can resume without double-charging.
decision_summary: We will use a hybrid HMAC-based certificate by default (backwards-compatible with API keys) and support asymmetric signatures later for customers who manage keys. Certificates will be short (base64 compact JSON), sent as an HTTP header `X-Usage-Cert` for minimal SDK changes. Ledger entries will be sharded per-customer and stored in a low-latency write-optimized store (per-customer Redis stream + append-only RocksDB per partition) with a TTL eviction of 30 days for auditability. Provisional quota reservations subtract from available quota immediately; the final commit reconciles estimated vs actual tokens and emits a reconciliation event for billing and analytics.
implementation_plan: Design certificate compact schema and canonical encoding (v1), include: client_id, digest(payload), client_nonce, estimated_tokens, ttl, issued_at, version
Add signer helpers to official SDKs (Node/Python/Go) and server-side HMAC verification library
Implement per-customer provisional ledger API (CreateCertificate, ResolveCertificate, RollbackCertificate) with idempotent semantics
Wire provisional reservation into quota subsystem and update rate limiter hooks to consider provisional reservations
Expose reconciliation events to billing pipeline and Redwood Console for troubleshooting
Run staged rollout: internal infra + canary customers -> opt-in beta -> gradual enforced validation
open_risks: Clock skew: clients with skewed clocks could issue TTLs that expire early or late — mitigate by allowing small skew window (±60s) and relying on issued_at + server-now checks
Key rotation: API key rotations may invalidate previously signed certs — plan rotation grace where server accepts signatures signed with previous keys for a configurable window
Performance: per-request ledger writes could increase tail latency under high QPS — optimize with batching and in-memory caching of recent certificates for fast-path dedupe
Client adoption: older SDKs may not send certificates; system must operate in backwards-compatible mode with heuristic dedupe but lower guarantees
Estimated tokens mismatch: clients can misestimate leading to provisional over-reservation; reconciliation must refund/adjust billing metrics
testing_plan: Unit tests: signature verification, canonical encoding, ledger idempotency semantics
Integration tests: end-to-end flow with provisional reservation + commit + rollback under simulated retries
Load tests: synthetic QPS with high retry rates to measure extra latency and throughput impact; validate caching reduces backend writes
Chaos tests: simulate partial commits, region failover, clock skew, and key rotation to validate durability and correctness
Customer trials: enable for a small set of customers with instrumentation to monitor duplicates and quota anomalies
notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after postmortem from incident INC-2026-02-18 where duplicate billing spikes were traced to SDK retries across an L4 proxy.
2026-02-24: Design review with Billing, Runtime, and SDK teams — consensus on header approach and HMAC default. Action: produce compact schema and SDK helper RFC.

2026-03-02: Spike implemented: Node SDK signs HMAC cert and server verifies; observed ~1.4ms median verification cost. Embedded PoC ledger used Redis streams; need next iteration for durability and cost.
2026-03-08: PM prioritization call: mark as P1 for next release window due to customer complaints from two enterprise customers. Assignee Diego to draft rollout plan.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged key-rotation and replay-window controls — added to open_risks and testing_plan.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Node/Python/Go) provide a signing helper and example integration
Server verifies certificate signature and records provisional ledger entry under 10ms median additional latency on canary
Duplicate billable ingestion rate is reduced by >=95% for retried requests in canary customers
Billing pipeline receives reconciliation events and final invoices reflect committed usage only
Runbook updated with steps to debug certificate failures, key rotation, and forced rollback
